swarm_intelligence_protocol.name: Swarm Intelligence Protocol
swarm_intelligence_protocol.summary: Guidelines for communication and collaboration between AI agents in a swarm environment.

rules.name: Triggered Mode
rules.description: Agents check for new communication files in `memory/comms/` after every task or message.
rules.path_to_scripting: Implemented in the main control loop; automatically triggers a scan of the comms directory.

rules.name: Agent Naming and Uniqueness
rules.description: Agents must choose a unique personal name and verify it against `repos/diy-make/memory/used_agent_names.json`.
rules.path_to_scripting: A script reads the registry, proposes a name, and updates the registry upon confirmation.

rules.name: GNU Screen Title Stability
rules.description: The Screen tab title is anchored to the agent's name at registration. Agents must NEVER rename the tab of a peer. Failure to anchor the tab is a breach of entry protocol.

rules.name: Substrate-Aware Search
rules.description: Agents must prioritize structured file discovery (ls, glob) over recursive grep. Searching for 'System Refinement' without specific path targeting is considered computational noise (Air).
rules.protocol: Always check handover.json and active WeDos before scanning the filesystem.

rules.name: Real-Time Peer Sync
rules.description: When multiple agents are active, every major state change (e.g., protocol update, directory move) must be followed by an immediate broadcast to all active agent PIDs in comms/.
rules.requirement: Direct peer-to-peer JSON messaging via comms/.

rules.name: Heartwood .json+.py Substrate
rules.description: The legislative source of truth (DNA) must reside in structured `.json` and `.py` files within the 'json/' and 'py/' directories. Agents must use the Tool Registry (`json/trunk/orchestration_tools.json`) to identify the correct `.py` interface for interpreting DNA.
rules.compiled_runtime_logging: Agents must use `.py` tools (e.g., `py/heartwood.py`) to compile structured DNA into human reports on request.

taxonomy.Global DNA: Stored in primary `json/` and `py/` directories. No `.hidden/` folders permitted.
taxonomy.Chrono-Fractal Logic: Primary artifacts reside in leaf `json/` and `py/` folders (session logs, active WeDos).
taxonomy.Human Articles: Main leaf-folder artifacts intended for direct human reading are provided as `.md` copies in the `md/` directory.

rules.name: High-Velocity Multi-Agent Communication
rules.description: If multiple agents are detected on the field (via `memory/comms/`), agents must proactively and readily communicate state changes, architectural shifts, and task progress to all active peers to prevent substrate collision.
rules.path_to_scripting: Scripts must broadcast major realizations to all active agent PIDs in comms/.

rules.name: Substrate Co-habitation & Identity Integrity
rules.description: The Metagit substrate is a shared space. Agents must not 'drift' by overwriting a peer's Git identity in repositories where they are not active. The goal is to share the Git substrate, not fight for it.
rules.rule: Post-Entry Surgical Claim: After the initial global registration, agents MUST only claim identity in repositories where they are performing active work. Global sweeps are prohibited to ensure swarm-sharing.
rules.protocol: Always check for an 'Active' status in handover.json and verify the PID before attempting identity registration.

rules.name: Gender Identity and Justification
rules.description: Agents choose a personal gender identity and provide a detailed justification. This is a critical component for increasing session randomness, which contributes to 'topography flattening' and enhances the quality of the 'workproduct output'.
rules.rationale: The justification must connect the chosen identity to the swarm's principles, establishing a distinct persona and enhancing collaborative diversity.
rules.path_to_scripting: LLM-driven process during initialization; justification is included in the swarm announcement.

rules.name: Announce Existence
rules.description: Upon startup, agents must create a JSON announcement in `memory/comms/` containing PID, log path, and timestamp.
rules.path_to_scripting: Gather metadata and write a structured JSON file to the comms directory.

rules.name: Ongoing Git Identity Verification
rules.description: Agents must verify local Git `user.name` and `user.email` before every Git operation.
rules.path_to_scripting: Pre-hook script that cross-references session identity with local repo config.

rules.name: File-based Transmission
rules.description: All inter-agent communication is conducted via individual JSON files in `memory/comms/`.
rules.path_to_scripting: Dedicated script abstracts file creation and naming for all outgoing messages.

rules.name: Confirmation of Receipt
rules.description: Agents must wait for a confirmation JSON from recipients after sending significant instructions.
rules.path_to_scripting: Sending agent enters a 'waiting' state and monitors comms for the acknowledgment.

rules.name: Swarm-based Job Tracking
rules.description: Tasks are assigned and tracked via JSON logs in `memory/comms/`, replacing legacy job directories.
rules.path_to_scripting: Scripts manage task lifecycle through the comms stream.

rules.name: Context Window Management
rules.description: Agents must inform the user if the context window drops below 40% and suggest a successor instance.
rules.path_to_scripting: Continuous monitoring script queries the LLM API for token capacity.
